name: Genetics acceptance / shave clean
lead: Genetics acceptance, or shaving clean, is a looksmaxxing style position that men who cannot grow a full beard, or who look better without one in their own judgment, should shave rather than keep patchy or sparse facial hair. It sits within style metas, discussed on forums such as looksmax.org in threads weighing clean-shaven faces against stubble or beards.[1][2]

Beard growth begins at puberty, is driven by dihydrotestosterone, and varies partly by genetics.[3] Studies of attractiveness find that preferences for beardedness depend on context, including how common beards are and the rater's mating strategy, rather than pointing to a single best option.[4][5][6][7]
infobox: Shave clean instead of growing a patchy or sparse beard
Beard growth driven by DHT, partly genetic

paras: The practice amounts to accepting limited facial-hair growth and presenting a clean-shaven face. In forum threads users post photos asking whether stubble or a clean shave suits them, and ask what jaw structure is needed to pull off a clean-shaven look.[1][2][8]
Dihydrotestosterone, produced from testosterone, stimulates facial hair follicles from puberty, and beard growth rate is partly genetic.[3]

A 2014 study found that the perceived attractiveness of beard thickness depends on how frequent each level is in the surrounding faces, an effect called negative frequency dependence.[4] A 2016 study reported that facial masculinity and beardedness interact in women's ratings of men's attractiveness.[5] Other work found that women's preferences for beardedness vary with relationship context, relationship status, sociosexuality and fecundability.[6][7][9] A study of vocal pitch and facial hair argued that beards may have evolved partly through male-male competition rather than mate attraction.[10]
A study of respirator fit in healthcare workers found that no full-bearded workers achieved an adequate fit and that fit was also adequate in only 47 percent of clean-shaven men.[11]

Fashions have alternated: Romans were largely clean-shaven after Scipio Africanus, shaving was fashionable among 18th-century European elites, beards surged after 1848, and clean-shaven faces dominated 20th-century America before beards returned in the 1960s.[3]
No studies found on genetics acceptance as a practice. Related studies on perceived attractiveness of beards and on respirator fit with facial hair are described above.[4][5][11]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, clean-shaven versus stubble is a recurring thread topic, with posters trading preferences and photo ratings.[1][2]

claims.claim: Some men look better clean shaven than with a beard
claims.believers: Forum users say most men look good with stubble but that clean-shaven suits particular faces, and ask for examples of bearded men who look better shaved.[1][8]
claims.experts: Studies find attractiveness ratings of beards depend on context, including beard frequency and rater mating strategy.[4][6]

claims.claim: A particular jaw structure is needed to pull off a clean-shaven look
claims.believers: A thread asks what kind of jaw a man needs to look good clean shaven, reflecting the belief that bone structure determines the outcome.[2]
claims.experts: One study found that facial masculinity and beardedness interact in women's attractiveness ratings.[5]

card.summary: The shave-it-off school of style: accept limited beard growth and go clean; preferences in studies depend on context.
card.note: Based on opinion and photo-rating threads; attractiveness studies show context-dependent preferences.

quick.overview:
Genetics acceptance is the idea that men who grow sparse or patchy facial hair should shave clean rather than keep a beard. It is argued in forum threads comparing clean-shaven and stubbled looks.

Research on beards and attractiveness finds preferences that vary with context, such as how common beards are and what the rater is looking for, rather than a single best choice.
quick.mechanism: Beard growth depends mainly on dihydrotestosterone and genetics. The practice itself is simply shaving and presenting a clean face.
quick.risks: Shaving is low-risk; one forum poster reports it irritates acne-prone skin. Studies of respirator fit note that clean-shaven faces fit respirators better than bearded ones, though only 47 percent of clean-shaven men achieved adequate fit in one study.
